item.title: Elon Musk to Owe Billions After Jury Finds He Misled Twitter Investors Before Takeover | KQED
item.description: A federal jury in San Francisco found Elon Musk liable for attempting to drive down Twitter’s stock price with misleading statements ahead of his 2022 acquisition of the company.

item.title: California's Political Reckoning With Cesar Chavez's Legacy After Allegations | KQED
item.description: A New York Times investigation into allegations of rape and sexual abuse of girls and women — including labor icon Dolores Huerta — by the late farmworker leader Cesar Chavez, sparked swift condemnation from California politicians and labor groups.

item.title: Judge Sentences Driver in Deadly West Portal Crash to 2 Years Probation, No Prison Time | KQED
item.description: The ruling comes almost exactly two years after Mary Fong Lau, 80, crashed into a bus stop at high speed, killing a family of four.

item.title: Which San Francisco Building Is the Hottest? This Website Wants Your Vote | KQED
item.description: A San Francisco tech founder created “Facade Mash,” a viral website where users rank the city’s most beautiful buildings — from Victorian homes to quirky architecture — drawing thousands of votes across the city.

item.title: Unsung Heroines: Rebel Girls of the Bay Area | KQED
item.description: San Francisco Bay Area history is full of women who had a powerful impact on the social, cultural and political life here. Rae Alexandra's new book Unsung Heroines: 35 Women Who Changed the Bay Area highlights the little known stories of these women.

item.title: The Lowrider Community’s Long Fight to Ride Freely | KQED
item.description: For decades, lowriding was blamed for traffic and alleged connections to gang violence. This month, lowriding is being honored with a federal stamp.

item.title: Despite Protections, The California Condor Struggles | KQED
item.description: Despite Lead Ammo Ban, CA Condors Keep Dying Condors are the largest land bird in North America. When their population shrunk to just 23, a substantial conservation campaign in California followed, spanning several decades. Now there are more than 600 alive, but they aren’t doing as well as scientists expected.
